hypotheses.claim: Biaxial strain of 15% applied to a TiO2-nanorod photonic crystal slab embedded in epoxy shifts the lattice constant from 330 nm to 280 nm, phase-matching the TE0 and TM0 guided modes of a 10 µm GaN micro-LED across 450–630 nm, yielding 47±2% EQE at 1000 nits.
hypotheses.mechanism: Mechanical deformation of the encapsulant matrix (generic_mechanism_9) directly stretches the ordered nanorod array (generic_mechanism_1), reducing the center-to-center spacing (generic_property_5) which shifts the Bragg diffraction condition (generic_property_8) to satisfy momentum conservation for guided-mode outcoupling (generic_process_10), thereby producing broadband extraction (generic_effect_11).
evidence: Chameleon iridophores tune guanine crystal spacing via cytoskeletal strain
Photonic crystal slab theory predicts guided-mode extraction at λ/n_eff ≈ a
Nanoimprint lithography demonstrates 280 nm period TiO2 rods in epoxy
assumptions: Epoxy modulus <500 MPa at 50°C enables uniform 15% biaxial strain
TiO2 nanorods (aspect ratio >3) survive strain without fracture
UV cure locks periodicity with <1% shrinkage
expected_failure_modes: Epoxy stress relaxation >5 nm periodicity drift post-cure
Delamination at GaN/epoxy interface during thermal cycling
hypotheses.novelty_rationale: Directly transfers the chameleon's spacing-tuning mechanism to a manufacturable strain-and-lock process for micro-LEDs, replacing physiological control with a one-time manufacturing step.
hypotheses.testability: Fabricate 10 µm micro-LEDs with strained encapsulant; measure EQE vs. wavelength and angle; map EQE uniformity across panel; thermal cycle -40°C to 85°C 1000×.
hypotheses.falsifier: If EQE remains ≤35% after 15% strain, or if periodicity measurement (SEM) shows <260 nm or >300 nm lattice constant, or if subpixel EQE variation exceeds 10%, this hypothesis is falsified.

hypotheses.claim: Uniaxial strain of 10% aligns initially isotropic TiO2 nanorods (diameter 80 nm, length 300 nm) into a birefringent layer with extraordinary index n_e=2.45, ordinary index n_o=1.85, creating polarization-selective outcoupling that boosts TE-mode extraction to 52% while TM-mode reaches 42%, averaging 47% EQE.
hypotheses.mechanism: Matrix deformation (generic_mechanism_9) reorients anisotropic nanostructures (generic_mechanism_1) rather than changing their spacing, modulating the effective refractive index tensor (generic_property_8) which enables polarization-dependent phase-matching (generic_process_10) to produce enhanced extraction (generic_effect_11).
evidence: Liquid crystal elastomers show strain-induced birefringence Δn>0.3
TiO2 nanorod alignment in polymer matrices demonstrated via stretching
GaN micro-LEDs emit predominantly TE-polarized light
assumptions: Nanorods have aspect ratio >3.5 to rotate under strain
Epoxy yields at <50°C allowing rod rotation without fracture
No significant periodicity change (<2%) during alignment
expected_failure_modes: Epoxy modulus too high for rod rotation
hypotheses.novelty_rationale: Exploits strain-induced orientational order (not spacing change) to create a birefringent extraction layer matched to the TE-dominant emission of GaN, a mechanism distinct from chameleon spacing tuning but rooted in the same matrix-deformation causality.
hypotheses.testability: Measure polarization-resolved EQE and angular emission; use polarized Raman to quantify nanorod order parameter; vary strain direction relative to pixel array.
hypotheses.falsifier: If polarization-resolved EQE shows <5% difference between TE and TM modes, or if Raman order parameter S<0.3 at 10% strain, or if EQE drops below 38% for either polarization, this hypothesis is falsified.

hypotheses.claim: Compressive pre-strain of 8% followed by UV cure creates a graded-index nanostructure layer where the local periodicity varies linearly from 260 nm at the GaN interface to 320 nm at the epoxy surface, enabling adiabatic mode transformation that extracts 49±2% EQE with <2% angular color shift.
hypotheses.mechanism: Controlled non-uniform deformation (generic_process_6 → generic_process_7) creates a spatial gradient in nanostructure spacing (generic_property_5) which produces a continuous shift in the interference condition (generic_property_8) across the layer thickness, enabling broadband adiabatic outcoupling (generic_process_10 → generic_effect_11) rather than discrete Bragg matching.
evidence: Graded-index anti-reflection coatings show broadband performance
Chirped photonic crystals demonstrate adiabatic mode conversion
assumptions: Strain gradient can be imposed via wedge-shaped stamp or pressure profile
UV cure freezes gradient before stress relaxation
Nanostructure density scales linearly with local strain
GaN guided modes couple adiabatically to radiation modes
expected_failure_modes: Stress relaxation smears gradient during cure
hypotheses.novelty_rationale: Transfers the spacing-tuning principle into a spatially graded architecture that solves the RGB broadband challenge via adiabatic transformation rather than single-periodicity optimization, leveraging the same deformation→spacing→interference causality in a continuous fashion.
hypotheses.testability: Cross-sectional SEM/TEM to map periodicity vs. depth; angle-resolved spectroscopy for color shift; thermal cycling with in-situ EQE monitoring.
hypotheses.falsifier: If cross-section shows periodicity variation <3 nm/µm (insufficient gradient), or if angular color shift exceeds 0.01 CIE Δx,Δy, or if EQE <43% despite gradient, this hypothesis is falsified.

distinguishing_predictions: Hypothesis 1 (periodicity tuning) predicts a single sharp Bragg peak in angle-resolved reflectivity at λ≈280 nm×n_eff that shifts uniformly with strain; Hypothesis 2 (nanorod alignment) predicts strong polarization anisotropy (TE/TM EQE ratio >1.2) with minimal periodicity change in SEM; Hypothesis 3 (graded index) predicts a broad, featureless extraction spectrum with linear periodicity gradient in cross-section and near-zero angular color shift. Measuring polarization-resolved EQE, cross-sectional periodicity mapping, and angular color shift simultaneously will uniquely identify the operating mechanism.
